engine_note: engine selects the backend class via main.py ENGINE_FACTORY; display_label is the descriptor-driven QAM/log label. Neither requires an if game=="stardew" branch. Adding a game = descriptor JSON only (plus a parser class only if the manifest FORMAT differs).

identity.name: Stardew Valley
identity.note: AppID 413150, native Linux build (no Proton prefix). SMAPI is an EXTERNAL launcher that the user has already installed and wired into Steam launch options. This plugin is DETECT-ONLY: it never installs SMAPI, never edits Steam launch options, never writes a Proton pfx, never uses a DLL override.

notes: SMAPI has NO game state file: enabling a mod == the mod DIRECTORY being present under Mods/. There is no ModsConfig.xml, no <activeMods>, no locked Core entry. state_file/state_staging are therefore null and all state-file preflight/snapshot/drift logic is skipped.

mod_root is the SMAPI Mods/ folder. Each SMAPI mod is a directory Mods/<dir>/ containing manifest.json. The install directory name is derived from the manifest UniqueID (sanitized), NOT from the ZIP name.
staging and quarantine are SIBLINGS of Mods/ (under GAME_ROOT), never inside Mods/. Quarantine stays on the same filesystem as Mods/ so os.replace never raises EXDEV(18).

COEXISTENCE (highest risk): a third-party Flatpak mod manager (io.github.Amethyst.ModManager) may deploy this Mods/ tree via symlinks, marked by Mods/.mm_deployed and a sibling Mods_Core/ directory. When either marker is present the plugin MUST run in READ-ONLY / DETECTION mode: status/list_inbox/inspect stay available, but install/set_enabled/uninstall/rollback return E_EXTERNAL_MANAGER. It must never move, rewrite, or unpack over symlinked mods or the Mods_Core/ tree.

loaders_note: SMAPI is detected, NEVER installed. detect.patterns / launch_requirements come from registry/loaders/smapi.json and are CHECKED (not applied). If the launcher is missing the plugin reports E_LOADER_MISSING; it does not install it, does not set launch options, does not request root.

loader_log.notes: READ-ONLY. The loader's summary block is the only evidence that a mod was actually accepted by the game rather than merely sitting in Mods/. Nothing here writes, fixes or reorders anything: a skipped mod is reported, never repaired. Patterns were transcribed from a real 150-line log; a log written in another dialect yields a reason string, never a guessed result.

running_detection.note: Read from /proc argv[0] only. The plugin matches an executable whose basename is one of running_process_markers, or whose path lies inside GAME_ROOT. It never matches a substring of a later argument, so a terminal sitting in Mods/ is not mistaken for the game. Running is reported as 'unknown', never as 'not running', when /proc cannot be listed. See deckymod/procs.py.

mod_package.json_dialect_note: Real SMAPI community manifests are JSONC: ModManifestBuilder emits /* */ header comments, and several ship arrays with trailing commas. The parser tolerates comments/trailing commas generically (no game field names); opted in per-descriptor here.
mod_package.field_aliases_note: SMAPI built-in mods (Console Commands, Save Backup) use the UniqueId casing variant. Aliases are copied onto the canonical key before required-field validation. Zero field names in .py code.
mod_package.field_map_note: ALL game-specific field names live here, never in .py engine/parser code. JsonMapParser consumes this map; dependencies may be strings or objects whose id is under any dependency_id_keys entry. Adding a JSON-field game = one descriptor JSON, zero engine changes.

id_extraction.note: SMAPI UniqueID legitimately contains dots (e.g. Pathoschild.Automate) and mixed case. The DIR name is a sanitized/lowercased form; the raw UniqueID is kept as the identity key.

supported_versions_extraction.note: Informational badge only. No version gating.

mod_package.allow_extensions_note: SECURITY POSTURE CHANGE (approved 2026-11-14): SMAPI mods are .NET assemblies, so .dll/.so/.dylib MUST be accepted. ONLY these three are relaxed. .exe/.msi/.bat/.cmd/.ps1/.scr/.com/.jar remain refused, and ALL structural guards (symlink/device/hardlink, path traversal, backslash, absolute path, duplicate, encrypted, zip-bomb ratio, entry/depth caps) remain in force. The archive is unpacked, never executed.
mod_package.notes: SMAPI mods ship as a directory with manifest.json. The plugin never executes archive contents.

import_roots.label: downloads
import_roots.note: Where the Game Mode browser saves files. A free Nexus account cannot download through the API, so this is the directory the user's own download actually lands in. READ ONLY: nothing here is ever created, moved, or deleted.

mod_package.import_roots_note: Reading these is a Round 42 addition, not a new capability claim. Game Mode has no file manager, so without them the panel could only ever show files the plugin fetched itself, and the 'download it in your browser then import it' flow was unusable. The inbox stays first; these are a read-only courtesy, declared per game rather than discovered by scanning $HOME.

conflicts.note: READ-ONLY. Two mods that ship the same relative path overwrite each other and the winner depends on load order. This reports the fact; it never reorders, renames or deletes anything. The ignore list is per-mod metadata that would otherwise label every pair of mods as conflicting.
conflicts.scope_note: SMAPI gives every mod its own folder, so two mods shipping config.json or i18n/zh.json are two unrelated files, not a collision -- measured on the device: 27 of 27 reported 'conflicts' were exactly those per-mod files. The honest conflict for this loader is a duplicate UniqueID, which the manifest scan already reports. Set scope to 'shared_tree' only for loaders that copy all mods into one directory (BepInEx, a game's own asset root).

quarantine.note: Round 54. allow_reclaim gates DELETEING quarantine folders the journal can no longer restore (see docs/QUARANTINE.md). Deleting is the only way to get the space back, and it is not undoable, so the RPC takes an explicit list of transaction ids and a second confirming call; nothing sweeps the folder looking for things to remove. Folders the journal still references stay restorable and are refused by name.

notes: SMAPI has no central enabled-mod state file. A mod is ACTIVE iff its directory is present under Mods/.
install == enable: unpacking the directory into Mods/ IS the enable step. There is no separate two-phase install-then-enable confirm.
disable/uninstall == moving the directory into quarantine (a sibling of Mods/ on the same filesystem). It is NOT deleted until an explicit future cleanup, which is out of MVP.
rollback == os.replace() the quarantined directory back into Mods/. There is no state-file snapshot to restore.
Because there is no state file, verify-on-open drift detection (RimWorld's E_STATE_EXTERNAL / V15) does not apply here.

conflict_policy.file_collision_note: If Mods/<dir>/ already exists and is not tracked in our journal -> E_FILE_COLLISION (refuse, never silently overwrite). Symlinked directories are never treated as safe to overwrite.

capabilities_note: network_download=true is the round-19 source wiring. Round 18 used a third-party mod-site API with a personal key; round 19 RETIRES that source (its free-tier download links answer HTTP 403, and the credential RPCs are gone) and replaces it with GitHub Releases plus a plain-https URL fallback. What is enabled is only the download-to-inbox half-chain (gh_search/gh_releases/gh_download/download_url). It does NOT lift the write posture. detection_only=true remains the approved read-only posture: on the real Deck an external mod manager owns the Mods/ tree, so the final engine.install() still returns E_EXTERNAL_MANAGER until the user completes the B prerequisite (remove Amethyst .mm_deployed/Mods_Core, migrate the 27 real MODs, authorize lifting read-only). enable_disable=true since round 25: a disabled mod is moved OUT of Mods/ into the sibling .decky-disabled/ directory (same filesystem, os.replace, nothing deleted) and moved back on enable; this is NOT uninstall, which parks the folder in .decky-quarantine.  No Workshop, no loaders install, no Proton prefix, no .exe installers, no root, no SteamOS read-only toggle, no universal one-click.

github.notes: Anonymous public API only: no token is stored, sent or required. Assets are resolved through /repos/{o}/{r}/releases/assets/{id} (302) and the bytes are fetched with the redirect host pinned to asset_hosts, so a redirected download can never leave the allow-list. The browser_download_url printed in release JSON is never used: github.com itself answers 502 on this device.

direct.notes: Escape hatch for mods published outside GitHub. The URL is validated (https only, no userinfo, default port, no private/loopback literal host) and the bytes land in the inbox only; the Mods/ folder is written exclusively by the engine's install().

nexus_metadata.notes: METADATA ONLY. Measured on this device with a real free-account key: mod info, file lists and the latest_added/latest_updated/trending listings answer 200, but download_link.json answers 403 for every free account ('this is for premium users only'), the API has no keyword-search endpoint (mods/search.json parses 'search' as a mod id -> 422), and every website page is behind a Cloudflare challenge. So this source browses and inspects, prints the mod page URL for the user to download in a browser, and imports the ZIP they get. It never claims to download a mod it cannot. Requires a key the user supplies in the panel; state is kept at ${DECKY_PLUGIN_RUNTIME_DIR}/nexus_api_key mode 0600 and is never returned to the UI.

known_limitations: DETECT-ONLY: depends on the user's ALREADY-CONFIGURED SMAPI install and Steam launch options. If SMAPI is missing or launch options are not set, the plugin reports an error; it does NOT install SMAPI or edit launch options.

COEXISTENCE: if Mods/.mm_deployed or a sibling Mods_Core/ is detected (Amethyst ModManager VFS deployment), the plugin switches to READ-ONLY mode and refuses every write with E_EXTERNAL_MANAGER. It never touches symlinks or Mods_Core/.
file_drop has no load-order or dependency solving. SMAPI itself resolves dependencies at runtime. Out of MVP.

GITHUB COVERAGE: downloads come from GitHub Releases. Popular mods whose authors publish only on mod-hosting sites have no GitHub release (the largest Stardew monorepo has none), so they cannot be fetched here; use the direct-URL field for those.
DIRECT URL: a user-supplied https link is downloaded as-is. There is no repository trust anchor and no catalog entry, so the manifest still decides whether the ZIP is acceptable.
No universal one-click install, no Workshop, no loaders install, no Proton prefix access, no .exe installers, no root, no SteamOS read-only toggle.
